    MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT &
    ENTREPRENEURSHIP

      National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme

       The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) is a flagship initiative
        launched by the Government of India on 19th August 2016 under the Ministry of Skill
       Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). The scheme aims to promote
        apprenticeship training across the country by providing financial incentives,
         technological support, and advocacy assistance to employers and training providers.

        Objectives:

          Promote Apprenticeship Training: Encourage establishments to engage apprentices
          by offering financial support.

               Skill Development: Enhance the skill levels of the workforce by providing on-the-job
             training opportunities.

          Employment Generation: Facilitate employment opportunities for youth through
             industry-relevant training.

       Implementing Agency:





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-1)                                                                                      4

Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE): The central body
            responsible for policy formulation and implementation.

           Regional Directorates of Apprenticeship Training (RDATs): Oversee the scheme's
            execution in Central Public Sector Undertakings and private establishments
            operating in four or more states.

            State Apprenticeship Advisers: Manage the scheme's implementation in State
            Public Sector Undertakings and private establishments within their respective states.

        Target:

         50 Lakh Apprentices by 2020: The initial goal was to train 50 lakh apprentices
            cumulatively by the year 2020.

          Eligibility Criteria:

           Age: Minimum 14 years (18 years for hazardous occupations).

           Educational Qualification: Minimum 5th class pass.

           Apprenticeship Contract: Must have a contract of apprenticeship with the employer.

       Key Components:

        Stipend Support:

          Reimbursement of 25% of the prescribed stipend, up to a maximum of ₹1,500 per
         month per apprentice, to all employers who engage apprentices.

        Basic Training Cost:

          Reimbursement of the cost of basic training up to a limit of ₹7,500 for a maximum of
         500 hours (approximately 3 months) to Basic Training Providers (BTPs) for
            apprentices who come directly without any formal training.

         Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT):

            Stipends are provided through DBT directly into the bank accounts of beneficiaries
             to ensure transparency and timely disbursement.

      National Skill Development Mission

       The National Skill Development Mission (NSDM) was launched on 15th July 2015 by
        the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India to create convergence across sectors and States in
        terms of skill training activities and for skilling at scale with speed and standards.

        Objectives:

           Mission Statement: To rapidly scale up skill development efforts in India by creating
          an end-to-end, outcome-focused implementation framework that aligns the
          demands of employers for a well-trained skilled workforce with the aspirations of
            Indian citizens for sustainable livelihoods.





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-1)                                                                                            5

Core Aim: To develop skills of unskilled and semi-skilled workforce in India, thereby
            creating livelihood opportunities for them.

         Institutional Mechanism:

       The NSDM operates through a three-tiered institutional structure:

           1. Governing Council:

        Chairperson: Prime Minister of India.

        Functions:

            Provides overall guidance and policy direction.

           Decides on sub-missions in high-priority areas.

           Reviews overall progress and development of mission activities.

         2. Steering Committee:

        Chairperson: Minister in Charge of Skill Development.

        Functions:

           Ensures implementation as per Governing Council's direction.

            Sets targets and approves the annual mission plan.

         3. Mission Directorate:

       Headed by: Secretary, Skill Development.

        Functions:

           Implements and monitors mission activities at the national level.

           Coordinates implementation of all decisions of the Governing Council and Steering
           Committee.

           Coordinates sub-missions and state efforts.

            Allocates resources to states and implementing agencies.

       Key Institutions:

           1. National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC):

         A not-for-profit public limited company under Section 25 of the Companies Act,
            1956.

            Set up by the Ministry of Finance in a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) mode, with
            the Government of India's shareholding at 49%.

           Acts as a catalyst in skill development by providing funding to enterprises,
           companies, and organizations that provide skill training.

            Current Chairperson: Mr. A.M. Naik.





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-1)                                                                                          6

2. National Skill Development Agency (NSDA):

            Established in 2013 under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.

          Has dual objectives of quality assurance and policy research in the skills space.

           Implements the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF).

            Secretary in the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship is the
            Chairperson.

         3. National Skill Research Division (NSRD):

            Set up under NSDA to serve as the apex body for providing technical and research
           support to the mission.

        Mission Strategy:

       The mission consists of seven sub-missions under its purview:

             Institutional Training: Focuses on strengthening training institutions to enhance skill
           development.

             Infrastructure: Aims to improve the infrastructure required for skill training.

          Convergence: Ensures convergence and coordination of skill development efforts
           across multiple stakeholders.

            Trainers: Focuses on the development of a quality training ecosystem, including the
             training of trainers.

          Overseas Employment: Aims to provide skill training aligned with international
           standards to facilitate overseas employment.

           Sustainable Livelihoods: Focuses on promoting sustainable livelihoods through skill
           development.

           Leveraging Public Infrastructure: Utilizes existing public infrastructure for skill
             training purposes.

          The power to identify sub-missions lies with the Governing Council.

    PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana

       The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), launched in 2015, is the flagship
       scheme of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). It aims to
        provide industry-relevant skill training to youth, enhancing their employability and
        promoting sustainable livelihoods.

        Objectives:

           Encourage and promote skill development by providing free short-term training
            courses.

             Incentivize youth through monetary rewards for skill certification.




GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-1)                                                                                                  7

Align skill training with the demands of employers for a well-trained workforce.

       Implementing Agency:

            National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), under the aegis of MSDE,
           implements PMKVY through accredited training centers across India.

       Launch Timeline:

        PMKVY 1.0 (2015-16): Initial launch with a focus on skill certification and reward.

        PMKVY 2.0 (2016-20): Expanded scope with a target to train 10 million youth over
             four years.

        PMKVY 3.0 (2020-21): Focused on new-age and COVID-related skills with an outlay
            of ₹948.90 crore.

        PMKVY 4.0 (2022-26): Emphasizes digital and industry 4.0 skills, integrating
             training with employment opportunities.

       Funding Pattern:

            Centrally Sponsored Centrally Managed (CSCM): Implemented by NSDC with 100%
             central funding.

            Centrally Sponsored State Managed (CSSM): Implemented by state governments
            with 75% central and 25% state funding.

       Key Components:

           Short-Term Training (STT): For unemployed youth and school/college dropouts.

           Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL): Assessment and certification of existing skills.

            Special Projects: Training in special areas not covered under STT or RPL.

           Target Beneficiaries

          1. Indian nationals aged 15-45 years.

          2. Unemployed youth or school/college dropouts.

          3. Possess Aadhaar card and bank account.

    PMKVY 3.0

          Launched on: 15th January 2021

            Ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)

            Objective: To support the local economy by equipping youth with demand-driven
                 skill sets, aligned with the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

       Key Objectives:

           Promote decentralization of skill training.





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-1)                                                                                          8

Empower youth with industry-relevant skills to improve employability.

           Support local economic growth by tailoring skill development to district-level needs.

           Promote self-employment, especially in post-COVID India.

        Implementation Framework:

           1. Decentralized Structure:

            Greater roles for States/UTs, District Skill Committees (DSCs), and local bodies.

         District-level planning based on skill gap analysis and local demand.

         2. Trainee and Learner-Centric Approach:

           Emphasis on flexibility, choice of job roles, and training quality.

             Integrates soft skills, digital literacy, and entrepreneurial training.

         3. Coverage and Target:

           Coverage: 717 districts across India.

            Target: Train 8 lakh candidates.

           Timeframe: FY 2020–21.

          Budget Outlay: ₹948.90 Crore.

       Major Components:

           1. Short-Term Training (STT):

            For school/college dropouts and unemployed youth.

           Courses aligned with the National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF).

         2. Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL):

            For individuals with existing skills to be certified.

            Includes orientation, bridge training, and assessment.

         3. Special Projects:

            For skilling under unique government initiatives or employer-specific needs.

       Key Features:

             Training and assessment are free for the candidate.

         DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) model to ensure stipend and other benefits reach
             trainees directly.

           Monitoring through Skill India Digital Platform for transparency and efficiency.

           Impact and Monitoring:

           Real-time performance monitoring through dashboards and centralized systems.





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-1)                                                                                          9

Emphasis on quality over quantity—strict training center accreditation and trainer
              certification.

    PMKVY 4.0

       The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0, launched in 2023, is the latest
          iteration of the Government of India's flagship skill development program. It aims to
       make the existing skill ecosystem more flexible, swift, and geared to meet current
        challenges and emerging needs through process simplification.

       Key Objectives:

             Simplify processes to make the skill development ecosystem more adaptable and
            responsive.

          Enhance employability of youth by providing industry-relevant skills.

           Promote inclusivity by targeting marginalized and vulnerable groups.

       Implementing Agencies:

            National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC): Responsible for overall
            implementation and coordination.

           Sector Skill Councils (SSCs): Promote industry connect through skill gap studies,
            curriculum development, facilitating On-the-Job Training, Training of Trainers and
            Assessors, and support in overall implementation of the scheme.

               Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH): A mobile-first digital platform designed to synergize
             India's skill development, education, employment, and entrepreneurship landscape.
                    It provides end-to-end digitalization of the training lifecycle.

       Types of Trainings:

           1. Short-Term Training (STT):

           NSQF-aligned courses ranging between 300–600 hours.

            Target Group: Candidates aged 15–45 years looking for fresh skilling, re-
              skilling/upskilling, out-of-education candidates, school/college dropouts, or
          unemployed youth of Indian nationality.

         2. Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL):

          Assessment and certification for candidates with prior learning experience or skills.

            Target Group: Candidates aged 18–59 years with prior learning experience or skills
              willing to get assessed and certified.

         3. Special Projects:

            Project-based short-term skilling initiatives that primarily meet the skilling needs of
            marginalized and vulnerable groups, difficult geographies, and specialized training





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-1)                                                                                                          10

courses likely to be offered outside of regular short-term skilling programs.

            Target Group: Marginalized, vulnerable groups, etc., requiring special attention or job
             roles with a focus on future skills, aged 15–45 years.

       Coverage and Infrastructure:

        PMKVY 4.0 is being implemented across 717 districts in India.

    SANKALP AND STRIVE Schemes

       The SANKALP (Skills Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion)
       and STRIVE (Skill Strengthening for Industrial Value Enhancement) schemes are flagship
          initiatives under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE),
        launched in October 2017 with World Bank assistance. Both schemes aim to enhance
        the quality and market relevance of skill development programs across India.

        Objective:

          To improve short-term skill training qualitatively and quantitatively by strengthening
              institutions, bringing in better market connectivity, and including marginalized
            sections of society into the initiative.

        Funding:

             Total outlay: ₹4,455 crore.

           World Bank loan assistance: ₹3,300 crore.

       Key Features:

             Institutional Strengthening: Focus on strengthening State Skill Development
           Missions (SSDMs) and District Skill Committees (DSCs) to ensure decentralized
            planning and implementation.

             Inclusivity: Priority given to underprivileged and marginalized communities,
             including women, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and Persons
            with Disabilities (PWDs).

           Entrepreneurship Development: Training programs conducted for beneficiaries,
          such as the Entrepreneurship Development Programme for 335 individuals in Goa.

    PM- Kaushal Kendra Project

       The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendra (PMKK) project is a flagship initiative under the
         Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), implemented by the
         National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC). It aims to establish state-of-the-art,
          visible, and aspirational model training centers across India to enhance the skill
       development ecosystem.

        Objectives:





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-1)                                                                                                                                        11

Establish Model Training Centers: Set up benchmark institutions that demonstrate
             aspirational value for competency-based skill development training.

               Skill Training for Youth: Provide short-term training (STT) modules to unemployed
            youth, enhancing their employability.

           Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL): Contribute to the capacity building of municipal
          employees by recognizing and certifying their existing skills.

            Integration with National Missions: Align with the Skill India Mission and the Smart
             City Mission to promote inclusive and sustainable development.

       Implementing Agencies:

            National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC): Responsible for funding support
          and overall implementation of the PMKK project.

        New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC): Collaborates with NSDC to leverage
             infrastructure and support skilling initiatives, especially in smart cities.

       Funding and Financial Support:

            Capital Expenditure Support: NSDC provides a secured loan of up to ₹70 lakhs per
        PMKK center.

         Interest Rates Based on District Category:

           Category A & B: 6% interest.

           Category C: 3% interest.

              Difficult Areas: 0% interest.

          Repayment Terms: The loan has a repayment period of 4 years, including a 1-year
           moratorium.

          Usage of Funds: Funds are allocated for training infrastructure, procurement of
           machinery and equipment, training aids, and internal renovations. They are not to be
          used for purchasing land or constructing buildings.

            Additional Support: For centers utilizing prefabricated structures, an additional loan
            of up to 75% of the project setup cost or ₹60 lakhs (whichever is higher) may be
            provided.

         Infrastructure and Facilities:

           Standardized Infrastructure: Centers are required to have a built-up area ranging
           from 3,000 to 8,000 sq. ft., depending on the district category.

          Smart Classrooms: At least one classroom equipped with audio-visual facilities and
             internet connectivity for virtual training, interactive sessions, and industry seminars.

           Counseling and Placement Cells: Dedicated rooms for counseling, mobilization, and
           placement coordination with industries and employers.





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-1)                                                                                                             12

Compliance and Inspection: Each center must be validated for compliance with
           mandatory infrastructure and branding guidelines before becoming operational.

         Integration with Smart City Mission:

       The PMKK project signifies an integration and convergence approach towards the Skill
         India Mission and the Smart City Mission. For instance, India's first PMKK for skilling in
        smart cities was inaugurated at Mandir Marg, New Delhi, in collaboration with NDMC.
        This center leverages NDMC infrastructure and caters to sectors like healthcare and
         solar energy, aiming to skill approximately 4,000 youth annually.

    Grameen Udyami Project

       The Grameen Udyami Project is a distinctive multiskilling initiative launched by the
         National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) in collaboration with Seva Bharti and
       Yuva Vikas Society. Its primary objective is to empower tribal youth by providing them
        with industry-relevant skills, thereby promoting inclusive and sustainable development
         within tribal communities.

        Objectives:

          Enhance Employment Opportunities: Equip tribal youth with skills that increase
              their employability.

           Boost Rural Economies: Stimulate local economies by fostering skilled labor within
               tribal regions.

          Reduce Migration: Provide local employment opportunities to minimize the need for
            migration to urban areas.

          Conserve Natural Resources: Encourage sustainable practices through skill
           development in areas like organic farming and forest-based livelihoods.

       Implementing Framework:

           Funding: Fully funded by NSDC.

           Implementation Partners: Seva Bharti and Yuva Vikas Society.

            Operational States: Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh,
           Jharkhand, and Gujarat.

          Program Under: Implemented under the Sansadiya Parisankul Yojana.

       Program Phases:

          Phase 1: Initiated in May 2022, targeting tribal youth in Maharashtra, Rajasthan,
            Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat. The program provided transportation,
            boarding, and lodging to ensure accessibility.

          Phase 2: Launched in August 2022 from Ranchi, Jharkhand, focusing on training
         450 tribal students in Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand. This phase emphasized

    PM Shram Yogi Maandhan Yojana

       The Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan Yojana (PM-SYM) is a voluntary and
         contributory pension scheme launched by the Government of India in February 2019. It
        aims to provide social security to unorganised workers by ensuring a minimum monthly
        pension of ₹3,000 after the age of 60.

        Objective:

          To offer old-age protection and social security to unorganised sector workers
           through a guaranteed monthly pension.

          Eligibility Criteria:

           Age: 18 to 40 years at the time of enrollment.

          Monthly Income: ₹15,000 or less.

          Employment: Engaged in the unorganised sector (e.g., street vendors, agricultural
            workers, domestic workers).

        Exclusions:

           Should not be covered under Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO),
           Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), or National Pension System (NPS).

           Should not be an income taxpayer.

        Contribution Details:

          The contribution amount varies based on the age at the time of enrollment. The
            subscriber contributes a fixed monthly amount until the age of 60, and the
          Government of India matches this contribution.

        Contribution Chart:





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-1)                                                                                                         14

Pension Fund Management:

          The Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) serves as the Pension Fund Manager,
            responsible for managing the pension fund and disbursing pensions to the
             beneficiaries.

      Scheme Benefits:

          Monthly Pension: ₹3,000 after attaining 60 years of age.

           Family Pension: In case of the subscriber's demise, the spouse is entitled to receive
        50% of the pension as family pension.

             Disability Benefit: If the subscriber becomes permanently disabled before 60 years,
            the spouse can either continue the scheme or exit and receive the subscriber's
             contribution with interest.

         Exit and Withdrawal Provisions:

             Exit Before 10 Years: Subscriber's contribution with savings bank interest will be
            returned.

             Exit After 10 Years but Before 60 Years: Subscriber's contribution with accumulated
              interest or savings bank interest, whichever is higher, will be returned.

          Death of Subscriber: Spouse can continue the scheme or exit and receive the
            subscriber's contribution with interest.

          Death of Subscriber and Spouse: The corpus will be credited back to the fund.

      Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana

       The Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana (ABVKY) is a welfare scheme administered by
        the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) to provide financial assistance to
        insured persons (IPs) who become unemployed. Initially launched in 2018, the scheme





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-1)                                                                                                             15

has been extended multiple times, with the latest extension covering the period from
        July 1, 2024, to June 30, 2026.

        Objective:

          To offer financial support to ESIC-insured workers during periods of involuntary
           unemployment.

          Eligibility Criteria:

            Insurable Employment: The IP should have been in insurable employment for a
          minimum of two years before unemployment.

        Contribution Requirements:

            At least 78 days of contributions in the contribution period immediately preceding
           unemployment.

            At least 78 days in one of the remaining three contribution periods in the two years
             prior to unemployment.

            Salary Limit: Monthly salary should be ₹21,000 or less. For specially-abled persons,
            the limit is ₹25,000 .

            Exclusions: Benefits are not available if unemployment is due to misconduct,
            voluntary retirement, superannuation, or termination under disciplinary action.

         Benefits:

             Relief Amount: 50% of the average daily wages payable for a maximum of 90 days
            of unemployment.

           Claim Submission: Claims can be submitted directly to the ESIC branch office
            without the need for employer certification.

           Waiting Period: Relief becomes payable after 30 days of unemployment.

     Deendayal Upadhyay Shramev Jayate Karyakram

       The Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Shramev Jayate Karyakram, launched on October 16,
        2014, by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is a comprehensive initiative aimed at reforming
         labor laws, enhancing transparency, and promoting skill development in India. This
       program supports the 'Make in India' campaign by creating a conducive environment for
          industrial development and ease of doing business.

        Objectives:

            Streamline labor law compliance to foster industrial growth.

          Enhance transparency and accountability in labor inspections.

         Empower workers through skill development and social security measures.

           Support the 'Make in India' initiative by improving the labor ecosystem.





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-1)                                                                                                            16

Key Initiatives:

           1. Shram Suvidha Portal:

         A unified web portal that assigns a Labour Identification Number (LIN) to
            businesses, facilitating online compliance for 16 out of 44 labor laws.

           Enables filing of self-certified, simplified single online returns, replacing multiple

             hospitals.

What Are Technical Textiles?

        Technical textiles are materials designed primarily for functional purposes rather than
         aesthetics. They are categorized into 12 segments based on their applications:
        Agrotech, Buildtech, Clothtech, Geotech, Hometech, Indutech, Mobiltech, Meditech,
        Protech, Sportstech, Oekotech, and Packtech. These textiles find uses in diverse fields,
        from agriculture and infrastructure to healthcare and defense.
